prompt.context: Heartcorp is a medical devices company that produces cardiovascular stents. They have developed a revolutionary product called Device X, which is the first of its kind and is positioned to replace all current products in the market. Heartcorp wants to launch Device X in Europe in the near future and then bring it to the U.S. in 6 months. They are 1 year ahead of the competition with regard to R&D of the product.
prompt.question: How do you determine what price to charge for Device X? What are the issues that need to be considered?

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost of an open heart surgery operation?
What is the frequency of repeat procedure using Device X?
What is the frequency of severe complication using Device X?
How many units of Device X will be necessary per operation?
Is the $2,000/unit willingness-to-pay figure a single data point or an average?

framework: Current price and rationale for existing product (value-based or cost-based pricing)
Benefits of Device X vs. old product: decreased side effects, fewer repeat procedures
Buyer willingness to pay (hospital purchasing departments, insurance payers, patient groups)
Cost of Device X (manufacturing cost per unit)
Total R&D cost (if not treated as sunk)

questions.prompt: Calculate the 'Cost Neutral Point' — the price at which the total cost to the hospital using Device X equals the total cost using the old product. Use the following data: Hospital cost per operation = $2,500; Old product cost = $500/unit; Units per operation = 2; Frequency of repeat procedure (old product) = 50%; Frequency of severe complication leading to open heart surgery (old product) = 30%.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize additional information is needed (cost of open heart surgery, Device X repeat/complication rates, units per operation for Device X), then build a side-by-side cost table and solve for the break-even unit price X.

math.setup: Set total expected cost with old product equal to total expected cost with Device X. Let X = price per unit of Device X. Units per operation = 2 for both. Open heart surgery cost = $15,000. Device X repeat rate = 0%, Device X severe complication rate = 5%.
steps: Old product — Repeat procedure cost: 50% x $3,500 = $1,750
Old product — Severe complication cost: 30% x $15,000 = $4,500
Device X — Repeat procedure cost: 0% x anything = $0
Device X — Severe complication cost: 5% x $15,000 = $750
math.answer: Cost Neutral Point = $3,250 per unit of Device X

questions.prompt: What factors might allow Heartcorp to price Device X above the cost neutral point?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify qualitative value drivers beyond the financial break-even calculation that justify a premium price.

questions.prompt: The company wants to sell Device X at a premium above $3,250/unit, but a survey of hospital purchasing departments shows willingness to pay of only $2,000/unit. What would you recommend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first clarify whether $2,000 is a single data point or an average (it is an average). Then propose two paths: (1) manage Heartcorp's expectations toward ~$2,000/unit, or (2) increase customers' willingness to pay through stakeholder engagement and clinical evidence.

questions.prompt: How can Heartcorp increase willingness to pay among hospital purchasing departments?
questions.guidance: Candidate should think beyond the direct buyer to other stakeholders who influence the purchasing decision, and to evidence-based strategies.

brainstorming.prompt: How can Heartcorp increase hospital purchasing departments' willingness to pay for Device X?

categories.name: Stakeholder pressure
ideas: Engage patient advocate groups to highlight reduced pain and lower complication rates
Work with insurance payers to demonstrate financial savings from fewer repeat procedures and open heart surgeries
Encourage insurers to adjust reimbursement rates to reflect Device X's superior outcomes

categories.name: Clinical evidence
ideas: Publish clinical trial results in JAMA or New England Journal of Medicine
Use peer-reviewed publications to convince physicians to advocate for Device X with hospital administration
Seek endorsements from leading cardiologists and professional associations

categories.name: Financial framing
ideas: Present total cost-of-care analysis showing net savings per patient to CFOs and finance departments
Model malpractice insurance premium reductions attributable to lower complication rates
Quantify inventory savings from needing fewer SKUs per procedure

categories.name: Pricing and contracting
ideas: Offer outcome-based or risk-sharing contracts tied to complication and repeat-procedure rates
Use tiered pricing or volume discounts to lower the perceived per-unit cost
Bundle with training and service contracts to justify premium positioning

recommendation: Set the launch price close to the cost neutral point of $3,250/unit, representing the maximum value delivered to hospitals on a pure cost basis
In parallel, pursue a willingness-to-pay elevation strategy so that future pricing can reflect the full value of Device X including soft benefits
risks: Hospitals may remain anchored to the $2,000 WTP figure even after stakeholder campaigns
Competitor entry within 12 months could erode pricing power before Heartcorp establishes market share
Regulatory delays in Europe or the U.S. could compress the 1-year competitive lead
next_steps: Commission a segmented WTP study across hospital sizes and geographies to identify pockets willing to pay above $3,250
Design a pilot outcomes-based contract with two or three anchor hospitals to build clinical evidence
Initiate publication process for Device X clinical data in high-impact medical journals
